steps.title: Gather all materials
steps.instruction: Collect the following items with catalog numbers: Glass micropipettes (Harvard Apparatus, GC150F-10), wood‑stick cotton tip swabs (Medline Scientific, 300230S), non‑sterile gauze swabs (Kruuse, 160120), surgery cover 60 × 90 cm (Kruuse, 141770), absorbent swabs (Kettenbach, 001911), non‑absorbable straight‑cutting suture needles (eSutures, Ethicon, K889H), 26 G × 16 mm hypodermic needles (BD Microlance, 304300), 23‑gauge needle (BD PrecisionGlide IM, 305145), Vetbond tissue adhesive (3M, 1469C), surgical glue (3M Vetbond, 372146), facial tissue (VWR, 115‑0600), bench liner paper (ScienceWare/VWR, 470145‑292), 8‑week‑old C57BL/6J mice (JAX, 000664), 100 % O₂, isoflurane (Baxter, 1001936060), lidocaine HCl (Sigma‑Aldrich, BP214), Betadine® surgical scrub (7.5 % povidone‑iodine), Xylocaine 1 %, buprenorphine HCl (Reckitt Benckiser, 0.3 mg ml⁻¹), carprofen (Canidryl, 122964), 0.9 % NaCl physiologic solution (Grovet/Braun, 99512), Viscotears liquid gel (Novartis, 2082642), 70 % ethanol, Sylgard (Sigma‑Aldrich, 761028‑5EA), NaCl (Sigma‑Aldrich, 433209 – discontinued), KCl (Sigma‑Aldrich, P9541), glucose (Sigma‑Aldrich, G8270), NaHCO₃ (Sigma‑Aldrich, S5761), MgSO₄·7H₂O (Sigma‑Aldrich, 63138), KH₂PO₄ (Sigma‑Aldrich, 92214), CaCl₂ (Sigma‑Aldrich, 449709), MgCl₂ (Sigma‑Aldrich, V000149), HEPES (Sigma‑Aldrich, H3375), reagents for Ringer’s solution and oxygenated modified ACSF (see Recipes).

steps.title: Prepare glass suction pipette
steps.instruction: Pull a glass capillary to obtain a pipette tip of 50–100 µm diameter, manually adapt the tip to the spinal cord, and connect the pipette to a vacuum pump through silicon tubing of increasing diameter for suction‑transection.

steps.title: Weigh mouse pre‑surgery
steps.instruction: Record the mouse’s weight before surgery and monitor it daily for the next 15 days to detect any postoperative weight loss.

steps.title: Induce anesthesia
steps.instruction: Place the mouse in a sealed induction chamber delivering 5 % isoflurane in 95 % O₂ until deeply anesthetized.

steps.title: Transfer and position mouse
steps.instruction: Move the mouse to the surgical area, place it ventral side down on a heating pad set to 37 °C, and maintain this temperature throughout the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Deliver 2 % isoflurane via a facial mask.
Verify absence of pinch‑evoked reflexes (pedal withdrawal).
Secure limbs with strips of tape, avoiding excessive stretch.

steps.title: Prepare surgical site
steps.instruction: Shave the back along the rostro‑caudal axis, apply sodium iodine (Betadine®) to the shaved skin for 5 min, apply eye ointment, avoid placing hands or instruments on the thorax, and cover the mouse with a surgical drape leaving a window over the incision site.

steps.title: Expose sacral segment
steps.instruction: Locate T12 vertebra using two fingers, make a longitudinal skin incision from ~T12 to L4, identify the L2 vertebral body (landmark for S2), and make a deep vertical incision with a small eye scissor to cut the ligamentum flavum between L1 and L2, revealing the dorsal artery.

steps.title: Apply local anesthetic
steps.instruction: Apply Xylocaine 1 % onto the exposed cord, wait ~30 seconds for effect, then use fine forceps to laterally position the dorsal roots.

steps.title: Aspirate S2 spinal tissue
steps.instruction: Using the prepared glass pipette attached to vacuum suction, start on one side of the cord and continuously aspirate the S2 segment until a complete discontinuity between rostral and caudal ends is observed, indicating removal of one spinal segment.

steps.title: Close wound and post‑op care
steps.instruction: Suture the paraspinal muscle, close the skin with veterinary glue, and administer post‑operative analgesia: buprenorphine 0.1 mg kg⁻¹, carprofen 5 mg kg⁻¹, and, if needed, 0.3 ml sterile 0.9 % NaCl subcutaneously for 2–5 days.

substeps.instruction: Turn off anesthesia and place the mouse in a cage on a heating pad for 1–2 h.
House the mouse alone for the first week, then optionally with a cage mate.
Monitor daily for distress, >10 % body‑weight loss, dehydration, or infection; consult a veterinarian if any occur.
Note that the lesion should cause only tail‑muscle paralysis; monitor bladder function for possible dysfunction.

steps.title: Evaluate lesion completeness
steps.instruction: After the experiment, dissect the spinal cord and visually assess the lesion (complete vs. incomplete) as described in Figures 1I‑L.

steps.title: Prepare dissection area for chronic mice
steps.instruction: Set up a clean, disinfected rodent‑surgery area with easy access to dissection equipment, similar to the lesion preparation area.

steps.title: Induce anesthesia for dissection
steps.instruction: Place the chronically lesioned mouse in an induction chamber with 5 % isoflurane/95 % O₂, confirm deep anesthesia, then transfer to the dissection table.

substeps.instruction: Check reflexes as before.
Place the mouse on bench liner paper, deliver 2 % isoflurane via facial mask, and re‑check reflexes.
Secure limbs with tape, shave the back, and clean the area with alcohol.

steps.title: Perform dorsal laminectomy
steps.instruction: Identify T12, cut skin from ~T12 to L5, remove overlying muscles and tendons, locate T13 spinous process, and start a dorsal laminectomy rostro‑caudally while perfusing the spinal column with cold (~4 °C) oxygenated modified ACSF at 20 ml min⁻¹ to reduce metabolism.

substeps.instruction: Cut left and right sides of the vertebral bodies with scissors, avoiding cord damage.
Maintain continuous flow of cold (~4 °C) oxygenated mACSF (20 ml min⁻¹).

steps.title: Isolate sacral spinal cord
steps.instruction: When the laminectomy is complete, deliver pure O₂ via facial mask for ~5 min, cut the skin at the abdominal muscle level preserving the abdominal artery, transect the cord at caudal lumbar levels, and cut ventral roots bilaterally to free the cord.

substeps.instruction: At the lesion site, carefully detach dura mater and spinal cord from the vertebral body.
Transfer the cord to a dissection chamber with continuous cold oxygenated mACSF flow (20 ml min⁻¹).
Remove the dura completely, then cut the cord and remaining dorsal/ventral roots to shorten the preparation.
Place the isolated cord in a Sylgard‑coated perfusion chamber and provide a continuous flow of mACSF at room temperature (3–7 ml min⁻¹).

steps.title: Set up in‑vitro recording chamber
steps.instruction: Move the cord to a recording chamber that has a Sylgard bottom and a Sylgard bridge, positioning the cord in an L‑shape (ventral side up) with the rostral end resting on the bridge and the caudal end pinned down.

substeps.instruction: Pin the ventral side from the caudal end for stability; use a bent minute pin as a hook for the rostral end.
Maintain a continuous flow of oxygenated Ringer’s solution throughout the experiment.
Connect suction electrodes to the ventral roots for motor‑activity recording and to dorsal roots for stimulation.
Lower the microscope objective over the region of interest for calcium imaging once electrodes are connected.

steps.title: Prepare Ringer’s solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve in distilled water to obtain the following final concentrations (pH 7.4, oxygenated with 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂, kept at 22–24 °C): 111 mM NaCl, 3 mM KCl, 11 mM glucose, 25 mM NaHCO₃, 1.25 mM MgSO₄, 1.1 mM KH₂PO₄, 2.5 mM CaCl₂.

steps.title: Prepare oxygenated mACSF
steps.instruction: Mix to obtain: 125 mM choline‑Cl, 1.9 mM KCl, 1 mM CaCl₂, 7 mM MgCl₂, 1.2 mM KH₂PO₄, 10 mM HEPES, 25 mM glucose; oxygenate with 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂, keep at ~4 °C.
